$comment: Read from the SIA chart set AD 2 LFML (AIP France, chart dated 2026-01-22): the reporting points come from the coordinates table of the chart,
the notes from the English column of its text pages, both read by a script and checked (each point lies within 80 NM of the aerodrome).
Only what the chart prints is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text. Drawings (circuit, routes, radials) are not read.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.
Procedures (arrivals, departures, special VFR, radio failure) were then structured by hand from the English column of the text pages; what the chart only draws is not recorded.

A "fr" object holds the French column of the same chart, copied as printed and never translated: a French note sits at the index of its English twin and is left empty when the twin could not be paired with certainty; the French of the procedures and of the points' purposes is not recorded.
name: Marseille Provence

source.extraction: chart text, table and English column read by script, procedures structured by hand
source.frenchExtraction: French column of the chart text, read by script and paired with the English sentences

reportingPoints.name: NA
reportingPoints.location: Ventabren, intersection of A8 and D19

reportingPoints.name: SB
reportingPoints.location: Junction of Bolmon pond and Marseille canal

arrivals.note: take note of the ATIS before contacting the ATC unit; request the clearance to enter the CTR at least 3 minutes before reaching the entry points; entry by LP, CB, E, SC or SW: contact Provence TWR

unless otherwise cleared or instructed by the ATS, overfly the entry points and follow the routings at the altitudes of the table; the routings printed on the VAC are likely to be imposed by the ATS; other routings and altitudes may be granted after pilot request and ATC clearance

arrivals.route: LP (1700 ft) or CB (2000 ft), then NA (1500 ft), then NB (1500 ft)
E (2000 ft), then EA (1500 ft), then NB (1500 ft)
SC (1500 ft MAX), then S (1500 ft), then SA (1500 ft), then SB (1500 ft)
SW (700 ft MAX), then S (1000 ft), then SA (1500 ft), then SB (1500 ft)

routes.route: SW (700 ft), then S (1000 ft), then SC (1500 ft MAX)
SC (1500 ft MAX), then S (1000 ft), then SW (700 ft)

arrivals.note: tell ATC the entry point in the CTR and the planned exit point, then comply with ATC instructions

departures.note: look at the ATIS before contacting the ATC unit: contact Provence Preflight, indicate the exit point and, when there is no flight plan, the flight data; the routings printed on the VAC are likely to be imposed by the ATC; other routings and altitudes may be granted after pilot request and ATC clearance

departures.route: NB (1500 ft), then NA (1500 ft), then LP (1700 ft) or CB (2000 ft)
NB (1500 ft), then EA (1500 ft), then E (2000 ft)
EB (1500 ft), then EA (1500 ft), then E (2000 ft)
SB (1000 ft), then SA (1000 ft), then S (1500 ft), then SC (1500 ft MAX)
SB (1000 ft), then SA (1000 ft), then S (1000 ft), then SW (700 ft)

withAts.axisCrossing: an explicit authorisation from Provence TWR must be obtained to cross the runway axes; failing that, hold at NB for a north to south crossing or at SB for a south to north crossing, without interfering with the axes
withAts.specialVfr: a special VFR clearance is necessary to enter the CTR at arrival, departure or transit when the observed conditions are: 1500 m <= visibility < 5000 m, and 600 ft <= ceiling < 1500 ft; special VFR by day only; to keep separation from IFR traffic, special VFR aircraft may be asked to hold
withAts.nightVfr: local flights inside the Provence CTR: no cloud below 2500 ft AMSL and visibility of at least 5 km; holding sectors: comply with ATC instructions; night VFR routes: comply with ENR 3.3.5

radio.failureOnArrival: squawk 7600; outside the CTR, do not enter it; inside the CTR, west of the runways leave the CTR by the routing via S (1000 ft) to SC, then climb to 1500 ft MAX; east of the runways leave by the most appropriate routing, either E (2000 ft) or NA (1500 ft) to LP (1700 ft) or CB (2000 ft)
radio.failureOnDeparture: before take-off do not take off; after take-off squawk 7600; west of the runways leave the CTR via S (1000 ft) to SC, then climb to 1500 ft MAX; east of the runways leave by the planned routing
radio.failureInTransit: outside the CTR do not enter it; inside the CTR leave it by the nearest VFR routing without crossing the runway axes

notes: Significant HEL activity in the AD traffic pattern or in the vicinity of the RWY.
For safety and security reasons, handling is compulsory for any ACFT, including ACFT going to the AIRBUS HELICOPTERS area.
List of handling services must be contacted before departure from origin AD: see AD 2 LFML TXT 06.
QFU 31L take-offs are prohibited when the crosswind component (including gusts) is greater than 12 kts on wet runway.
Large gathering of birds on the platform and close nearby.
Marked pylon day and night, North-East of the axis between the pond and the General Aviation Terminal (see AD 2 LFML ATT 01).
Taxiing prohibited except on RWY and TWY.
Traffic surveillance equipment: aerodrome equipped with primary and secondary surveillance radar.
Pour des raisons de sécurité et de sûreté l'assistance est obligatoire pour tous les ACFT, y compris les ACFT à destination du site AIRBUS HELICOPTERS.
Liste des assistants à contacter impérativement avant le départ du terrain d'origine : voir AD 2 LFML TXT 06.
Les décollages QFU 31L sont interdits lorsque la composante traversière du vent (y compris en rafales) est supérieure à 12 kt sur piste mouillée.
Pylône balisé jour et nuit sur AD, au Nord-Est des axes entre étang et Terminal Aviation Générale (voir AD 2 LFML ATT 01).
Equipement de surveillance du trafic : aérodrome équipé d'un radar primaire et secondaire.
